RWU7: Akal Purakh is One, and He is met through the grace of the Satguru.
One Universal Creator God. By The Grace Of The True Guru:
There is but one God. By true Guru is grace. He is obtained.
2PQF: The bani 'Chhant' of Guru Ramdas Ji, in Rag Asa, Ghar 4.
Aasaa, Fourth Mehl, Chhant, Fourth House:
5006: Bhinne = are soaked, have become wet, have come into a glow. Loin = eyes. Premi = in the love-colour. Ratanna = dyed, has been coloured.
My eyes have come into a glow with the Hari-Nam-water that gives spiritual life; my mind has been dyed in the love-colour of Prabhu.
My eyes are wet with the Nectar of the Lord, and my mind is imbued with His Love, O Lord King.
My eyes are wet with God s elixir and my soul is imbued with his love, O Lord.
O Hari Ram Raje! By the amrit of Your Nam our eyes are soaked, and the mind is (ratanna) dyed in Your love.
2H1C: Rami = Ram has. Kanchanu = gold. Sovinna = suvann, of fair colour.
Parmatma has rubbed my mind upon the touchstone (of His own Nam), and it has become pure gold.
The Lord applied His touch-stone to my mind, and found it one hundred per cent gold.
My master applied his touch-stone to my soul and found it hundred percent gold.

O Ram! The mind set upon the touchstone which is Your Nam becomes (sovinna) of excellent colour, or gold purified by a hundred firings. Gold of twelve firings is called pure; this is gold assayed and purified by a hundred firings — the sense being, it has become possessed of the highest bliss.
Z0WT: Gurmukhi = by taking the Guru's shelter. Chalulia = has been dyed with deep crimson. Tano = tanu, body, heart.
By taking the Guru's shelter my mind has become deep crimson in Prabhu's love-colour; my mind is drenched, my heart is drenched.
As Gurmukh, I am dyed in the deep red of the poppy, and my mind and body are drenched with His Love.
Through the Guru I am dyed deep red and my mind and body are wet with Lord is love.
By way of the Gurus my mind and body are soaked in the deep dye — the sense being, in the bliss of the atma.

Z41R: Muski = with musk. Jhakolia = has become thoroughly perfumed. Dhanu dhanna = fortunate, fruitful ||1||
(By the Guru's grace) servant Nanak has become thoroughly perfumed with the musk (of Prabhu's Nam); (servant Nanak's) whole life has become fortunate. ||1||
Servant Nanak is drenched with His Fragrance; blessed, blessed is his entire life. ||1||
Slave Nanak is soaked in Lord's perfume and blessed is his entire life.
Sri Guru Ji says: my mind has (jhakolia) mingled in the (muski) fragrance which is Your praise; by that, this whole human birth has become fit for the greatest blessedness. ||1||
5N5B: Aniale = having a point, (arrows) with sharp points.
The Gurbani that produces love for Prabhu's feet has pierced my mind, as arrows with sharp points pierce (a thing).
The Bani of the Lord's Love is the pointed arrow, which has pierced my mind, O Lord King.
The hymn of God's love is the pointed arrow which has smitten my heart O Lord.
O Hari Ram Raje! Your bani full of love, which is (aniale) arrows with barbed points — by those the mind has been slain.
AAX6: Pir = pain, ache. Piramm = love. Jaria = it is borne.
That man within whom the pain of Prabhu's love arises, he alone knows how it can be borne.
Only those who feel the pain of this love, know how to endure it.
He alone who feels the pain of love know how to endure it.
He to whom the pain of love has come — he alone who bears it knows.
030C: Jivan mukati = free of Maya's bonds even while doing the work of the world. Mari = having died, having become untouched by Maya.
That man who lives the spiritual life, untouched by the attachment to Maya, remains free of Maya's bonds even while doing the work of the world.
Those who die, and remain dead while yet alive, are said to be Jivan Mukta, liberated while yet alive.
He how effaces his ownself and is dead in life is said to have been emancipated while alive.
(Mari jivai) He who has died to the sense of being a separate self through the updesh of those who are gurmukhs, he alone is called jivan mukat.
L3ET: Dutaru = that which is hard to cross ||2||
O servant Nanak! (Say —) O Hari! Unite me with the Guru, so that I may cross this world (-ocean), which is hard to cross. ||2||
O Lord, unite servant Nanak with the True Guru, that he may cross over the terrifying world-ocean. ||2||
O God unit servant Nanak with the true Guru that be may cross the arduous world-ocean.
Sri Guru Ji says: O Hari! Unite me with such a Satiguru as by whom the hard-to-cross world may be crossed. ||2||
FSJ9: Mugadh = foolish, senseless. Govind = O Govind! Ranga = one who performs many plays and shows.
O Govind, master of countless wondrous plays! Meet (us); we, foolish and senseless, have come to Your shelter.
I am foolish and ignorant, but I have taken to His Sanctuary; may I merge in the Love of the Lord of the Universe, O Lord King.
I ignorant and stupid have entered Guru is asylum may I be blessed with Lord's love
O Ram Raje Govind! We, foolish, (mugadh) children, or more foolish than fools, have come into Your shelter. (Ranga) O You whose form is bliss! Unite us with Yourself.
DW5K: Guri = by way of the Guru. Manga = mangan, I beg.
I beg (of the Guru the gift of) the bhagti of Parmatma, (because) it is only by way of the perfect Guru that Parmatma can be met.
Through the Perfect Guru, I have obtained the Lord, and I beg for the one blessing of devotion to the Lord.
Through the perfect Guru I have obtained God and I pray for the devotional service of God alone.
O Hari! From the perfect Gurus, having begged the one bhagti of Yours, I have obtained You, Hari.
YTAB: Sabadi = by way of the Guru's shabad. Vigasia = has come into blossom. Japi = having remembered. Anat taranga = of infinite waves, in which countless waves are rising.
By way of the Guru's shabad, having remembered (the ocean-Prabhu) of boundless waves, my mind has come into blossom, my heart has flowered.
My mind and body blossom forth through the Word of the Shabad; I meditate on the Lord of infinite waves.
By Guru's hymns my soul and body have bloomed and I meditate on the Lord of endless (infinite) waves.
O (anat taranga) assumer of countless forms! By repeating You through the Guru's shabad, my (tanu) subtle mind and my body have (vigasia) blossomed.
QZ8P: Mili = having met {the difference between the words 'milu' and 'mili' is worth remembering} ||3||
O Nanak! (Say —) Having met the sant jan, in the company of the sants I have found Parmatma. ||3||
Meeting with the humble Saints, Nanak finds the Lord, in the Sat Sangat, the True Congregation. ||3||
On meeting the holy men Nanak obtained God in the society of saints.
Sri Guru Ji says: O Hari! Having joined the satsang of the sant jan, I have obtained You. ||3||
S2LT: Daial = O house of mercy! Prabh = O Prabhu! Hari raia = O Prabhu the Emperor!
O You who show mercy to the humble! O Hari! O Prabhu! O Prabhu the Emperor! Hear my supplication.
O Merciful to the meek, hear my prayer, O Lord God; You are my Master, O Lord King.
O God compassionate to the poor heart my supplication O God, you are my Lord and my King.
O Ram Raje, Hari Rai, Hari Prabh, merciful to the humble! Hear one supplication of mine.
EKJP: Hau = I. Magau = magaun, I beg. Sarani = support, shelter. Mukhi = in the mouth.
O Hari! I beg the support of Your Nam. O Hari! (If Your mercy be, then Your Nam) I can put into my own mouth (can repeat it with the mouth).
I beg for the Sanctuary of the Lord's Name, Har, Har; please, place it in my mouth.
I pray for the refuge of God s Name O my Lord God! put it into my mouth.
O Hari! I beg the shelter of Your Nam, by which the jap of Hari Hari may be put into my mouth; may I keep putting the amrit of the Hari Hari Nam into my mouth.
9FY8: Bhagati vachhalu = one who loves bhagti. Biradu = disposition from the very beginning. Laj = honour.
It is Parmatma's disposition from the very beginning that He loves bhagti; (whoever comes to His shelter) He keeps that one's honour.
It is the Lord's natural way to love His devotees; O Lord, please preserve my honor!
To love His devotees is the inherent disposition of God save my honour O Lord.
O Hari, lover of bhagats! This is Your (birad) vow; (Hari) whoever comes to Your shelter, You have gone on keeping that one's honour.
9607: Nami = by way of the Nam ||4||8||15||
Servant Nanak (too) has come to that Hari's shelter; (the man who comes to His shelter) Hari joins to His own Nam and carries across (the world-ocean). ||4||8||15||
Servant Nanak has entered His Sanctuary, and has been saved by the Name of the Lord. ||4||8||15||
Servant Nanak has entered yours sanctuary O God and your Name has saved him.
Sri Guru Ji says: O Hari, possessor of the Nam! By the Nam You have ferried the bhagats across; therefore I am in Your shelter — ferry me across as well. ||4||8||15||
JSQU: Gurmukhi = taking the Guru's shelter. Ladha = has been found.
Taking the Guru's shelter, searching and searching, I have found the friend-Prabhu (within my own self).
As Gurmukh, I searched and searched, and found the Lord, my Friend, my Sovereign Lord King.
Searching and seeking through the Guru I have found out God the friend.
(Dhundhi) Searching out the road, by way of the Gurus I have (ladha) found Hari Ram Raje the friend. Where have I found Him?
HPU6: Kanchan kot garh = a fort of gold. Kaia = body. Sidha = sidha, manifest.
This body-fort of mine has become (as it were) of gold, (because by the Guru's grace) Parmatma has become manifest within it.
Within the walled fortress of my golden body, the Lord, Har, Har, is revealed.
Within the walled castle of my golden body the Lord God is revealed.

That (kaia) fort which is the body, worth a crore of gold — that is to say, priceless — within that, by all the proofs, (hari) Hari has been established. As in: ☬ 'Bahar dhudhan te chhut pare gur ghar hi mahi dikhaia tha.'
E839: Vidha = has been pierced. Dhuri = from the very court.
(Within my own self) Parmatma's Nam-jewel, Parmatma's Nam-diamond (has been found), by which my (hard) mind, my (hard) heart has been pierced (has become soft).
The Lord, Har, Har, is a jewel, a diamond; my mind and body are pierced through.
The Lord master is a jewel and ruby wherewith my soul and body are pierced.
The Hari Hari Nam is itself this diamond and jewel, which has pierced my mind and body; or, in it my mind and body have been merged.
KVVG: Rasi = in the relish, in the bliss. Gudha = I have been steeped ||1||
O Nanak! (Say — O brother!) From the very presence of Prabhu, by great good fortune, Parmatma has been met by me; my own self has been steeped in the relish of His love. ||1||
By the great good fortune of pre-ordained destiny, I have found the Lord. Nanak is permeated with His sublime essence. ||1||
Predestined as very fortunate I have obtained God. Nanak is kneaded with His Nectar.

Sri Guru Ji says: when from the beginning my merits were great, then I obtained Hari. And again, in this relish of Hari my mind has been (gudha) kneaded in — the sense being, it has become undivided. ||1||
2NC8: Panthu = road. Dasava = dasavan, I ask. Mundh = the soul-bride. Jobani = (intoxicated) in youth. Bali = artless.
O Satiguru! I, the youth-intoxicated and artless soul-bride, stand always (at Your door) and ask (of You) the road (to the country of the Husband-Prabhu).
I stand by the roadside, and ask the way; I am just a youthful bride of the Lord King.
I, a girl like youthful bride of my Lord the king stand ever and inquire the road to him.
I, the (mundh) woman possessed of youth and of the highest love, stand daily and attentively asking the (panthu) road of Hari, Ram Raje.
HNKC: Gur = O Guru! Chetai = cause to remember. Margi = upon the road. Chali = may I walk.
O Satiguru! Keep making me remember the Nam of the Husband-Prabhu; (show mercy) that I may walk upon the road (that reaches Parmatma's country).
The Guru has caused me to remember the Name of the Lord, Har, Har; I follow the Path to Him.
The Guru has caused me to remember the Name of Lord God and I now tread the way to God.
O Guru! Cause me to make the simran of the Hari Hari Nam, by which I may become one able to walk upon Hari's road.
94AE: Mani = in the mind. Tani = in the heart. Adharu = support. Bikhu = poison. Jali = jalin, may I burn, may I burn away.
In my mind, in my heart, Prabhu's Nam alone is the support (if Your mercy be, then by the grace of this Nam) may I burn away the poison of haumai from within me.
The Naam, the Name of the Lord, is the Support of my mind and body; I have burnt away the poison of ego.
Within my mind and body is the support of the Name and I have burnt down the poison of pride
In my mind and in my body the Nam alone is the support; the poison of I-ness and mine-ness I have burnt away.
U0TA: Meli = may I meet. Banvali = Parmatma ||2||
O servant Nanak! (Say — O Prabhu! Unite me with) the Guru! Whoever has met Parmatma has met Him only by way of the Guru. ||2||
O True Guru, unite me with the Lord, unite me with the Lord, adorned with garlands of flowers. ||2||
O my God unite servant Nanak with true Guru who himself is united with the flower-bedecked Lord.
Sri Guru Ji says: unite me with that Satigur, O Hari Banvali! whom You have met.
2KEE: Gurmukhi = by way of the Guru. Piare = O beloved Hari! Mai = to me.
O beloved Hari! Come and meet me, long separated, by way of the Guru.
O my Love, come and meet me as Gurmukh; I have been separated from You for so long, Lord King.
Through the Guru come and meet me O my beloved since long I have been separated from you.
O Ram Raje, Beloved! Come and meet me, separated for a long age, by way of the Gurus.
AZMN: Bairagia = has become desolate. Rasi = with the (love) water. Bhinne = soaked.
O Hari! My mind, my heart is greatly desolate; my eyes are soaked with (Your) love-water (because of the separation).
My mind and body are sad; my eyes are wet with the Lord's sublime essence.
My mind and body are gone very sad My eyes are moist with God's ambrosia.
Without meeting, my mind and body have become greatly (bairagia) desolate. O Hari! My eyes stay soaked in Your relish — that is to say, they stay wet.
JNUZ: Mili = having met. Manne = may it be satisfied, may it take assurance.
O Hari! Give me word of the beloved Guru; having met the Guru, may my mind grow accustomed to Your remembrance.
Show me my Lord God, my Love, O Guru; meeting the Lord, my mind is pleased.
My Guru show me the Lord God my love meeting Him my mind is pleased.
O Guru! Tell me of the beloved Hari Prabh, that, O Hari! having met with You my mind may (manne) be satisfied.
6PBQ: O Nanak! (Say —) O Hari! I am a fool; join me to Your own work (of the simran of the Nam). ||3||
I am just a fool, O Nanak, but the Lord has appointed me to perform His service. ||3||
Me a fool Guru Nanak has appointed to perform the service, the service of God.
Sri Guru Ji says: set me, a fool, to the work which is the bhagti of Hari; then we shall be of some use.(1) ||3||
1MJB: Gur dehuri = the Guru's fair body. Amrit = the Nam-water that gives spiritual life. Burke = he sprinkles (into the hearts and bodies of others).
The Guru's fair heart stays always soaked with the Nam-water that gives spiritual life; that (Guru goes on sprinkling this) Nam-water that gives spiritual life (into the hearts of others as well).
The Guru's body is drenched with Ambrosial Nectar; He sprinkles it upon me, O Lord King.
The Guru's body is drenched with the nectar of God the King and he has sprinkled the Lord's nectar on me.
The body of the Gurus is soaked with the Nam of Ram Raje, and the Guru gives (burke) sprinklings of the amrit of Hari's Nam — that is to say, he gives the updesh.
7KBS: Mani = in the mind. Bhaia = bhai, became dear. Amriti = with the amrit, with the water that gives spiritual life. Chhaki chhake = chhaki chhaki, enjoying and enjoying.
Those men to whom the Satiguru's bani becomes dear within their own mind — enjoying and enjoying the relish of the bani, their hearts too become soaked with the Nam-water that gives spiritual life.
Those whose minds are pleased with the Word of the Guru's Bani, drink in the Ambrosial Nectar again and again.
They to whose soul the Guru's hymns are pleasing continually quaff the nectar.
Those to whom the Guru's bani seems good within their own mind, their minds become of one substance with the Nam-amrit.
3B62: Tuthai = by becoming merciful. Chuke = have come to an end. Dhak dhake = the daily shoves, the daily stumbles.
On the Gurus becoming pleased I have obtained Vahiguru, and now I shall not be shoved about.
As the Guru is pleased, the Lord is obtained, and you shall not be pushed around any more.
The Guru being pleased I have obtained God and shall no more be pushed and buffeted.
Those who have obtained Hari by the pleasedness of the Gurus, their (dhak dhake) doubts have been released.
ZWJD: O Nanak! Parmatma and Parmatma's servant become of one form; the servant is absorbed into Parmatma. ||4||9||16||
The Lord's humble servant becomes the Lord, Har, Har; O Nanak, the Lord and His servant are one and the same. ||4||9||16||
Lord s slave becomes the Lord God O Nanak the Lord and his slave are one.
Sri Guru Ji says: the servants of Hari, by repeating the Hari Nam, have become one with Hari — that is to say, they have become undivided. ||4||9||16||
732T: The treasuries of the Prabhu-bhagti that gives spiritual life are with the Guru, the Satiguru, alone.
The treasure of Ambrosial Nectar, the Lord's devotional service, is found through the Guru, the True Guru, O Lord King.
With the great True Guru is the treasure of God's ambrosial devotional service.
(Gur) With those great ones who are the Satigur is the treasury of the amrit which is the bhagti of Hari Ram Raje.
EDD3: Sacha sahu = the banker of the ever-abiding Nam-treasury. Sikh = to the Sikhs. Dei = he gives. Rase = rasi, capital, stock.
The banker of this ever-abiding treasury of Hari-bhagti is the Guru, the Satiguru, alone; he gives this capital of bhagti to his own Sikhs.
The Guru, the True Guru, is the True Banker, who gives to His Sikh the capital of the Lord.
The great True Guru is the True banker who gives his disciple the Lord s capital.
The worshipful Satiguru is the true banker; he gives to the Sikh the (rase) capital which is the Hari Nam.
SDLT: (The trade of Prabhu-bhagti) is the highest trade; fortunate is that man who carries on this trade; the Guru, the banker of the Nam-wealth, gives that man his applause.
Blessed, blessed is the trader and the trade; how wonderful is the Banker, the Guru!
Blessed, blessed is the trader and the trade, and all honour is into Guru, the merchant.
Blessed is the (vanaju) commerce of the Hari Nam, and to the (guru) banker also is (sabase) thanksgiving, who has such trade carried on.
UMK0: Jin lilati = upon whose forehead. Dhuri = from the very court. Likhase = has been written ||1||
Servant Nanak says: it is obtained only by those men upon whose forehead the writ (of the obtaining of this capital) has been inscribed from the very presence of Prabhu. ||1||
O servant Nanak, they alone obtain the Guru, who have such pre-ordained destiny written upon their foreheads. ||1||
O slave Nanak, they alone obtained Guru who have such a pre-ordained writ on there forehead.
Sri Guru Ji says: such a Satigur has been obtained by those upon whose (lilati) forehead a good writ has been inscribed from the very beginning. ||1||
Q6G8: Sachu = ever-abiding. Dhani = master. Sabhu = whole.
O Prabhu! You are our Master, You are our ever-abiding banker; this whole world (of Your creating) has come here to trade in the Nam with the Nam-capital You gave.
You are my True Banker, O Lord; the whole world is Your trader, O Lord King.
You, O my Master, are the True Banker, and the whole world is a dealer of Yours.
O Ram Raje, true banker! You are our (dhani) Master, and the whole world is Your trader.
9JUW: Bhande = bodies. Tudhai = You alone. Hari = O Hari! Thara = Yours alone.
O Prabhu! All these beings and creatures You alone have created; within them is the life-thing You Yourself have given.
You fashioned all vessels, O Lord, and that which dwells within is also Yours.
All the vessels You have fashioned and the thing within, is also Yours, O God.
All the (bhande) bodies You have made; O Hari! Within them the thing is (thara) Your own form.
LW84: Pavahi = You put. Sa = that alone.
No poor being can do anything at all (by his own effort); whatever thing (virtue or fault) You put into these bodies, that alone comes out.
Whatever You place in that vessel, that alone comes out again. What can the poor creatures do?
The thing which You puts into the vessel, that alone comes out. What can any.

Whatever thing is put into a vessel, that alone comes out; in this what reflection will anyone else make? The sense being this, that apart from Brahm there is nothing else at all; 'sabh gobind hai sabh gobind hai' — this will be established.

C7KD: O Hari! To Your servant Nanak too it is You alone who (showing mercy) have granted the treasury of Your own bhagti. ||2||
The Lord has given the treasure of His devotional worship to servant Nanak. ||2||
To servant Nanak, God has donated the treasure of His love-adoration.
Sri Guru Ji says: to me, Your servant, O Hari! You have given in every way the (bhandara) treasury which is Your own bhagti. ||2||
CLG9: Ham = we beings. Vitharah = we can tell in detail. Kia gun = which virtues? Suami = O Master! Apar = He beyond whom there is no other. Apar = He whose far shore cannot be found.
O my Master! (You are the master of boundless virtues) which of Your virtues can we count and tell? You are boundless, You are boundless.
What Glorious Virtues of Yours can I describe, O Lord and Master? You are the most infinite of the infinite, O Lord King.
What merits of Yours can I narrate O Lord? You are the remotest of the remote Master, the king.
O Master, Ram Raje! Which of Your virtues shall we set out in detail? You indeed are apar and apar.
0PZ5: O Master! We perform the praise of Your Nam alone night and day; this alone is the support of our life, this alone the prop.
I praise the Lord's Name, day and night; this alone is my hope and support.
God's Name, I praise day and night, and this alone is my hope and support.
O Hari! We perform the glory of Your Nam alone night and day, and of the Nam alone we keep the support with body and mind.
4Q7S: Kichhua = anything at all. Na janha = we do not know. Kiv = how? Pavah = may we find. Paro = the far shore, the limit.
O Prabhu! We are fools, we have no understanding at all; how can we find Your limit?
I am a fool, and I know nothing. How can I find Your limits?
I am a fool and know nothing. How can I find Your limit?
O Master! We fools know no sadhan at all; how shall we find the far shore of the world-ocean?
S6V8: Servant Nanak is the servant of Parmatma, the servant of Parmatma's servants. ||3||
Servant Nanak is the slave of the Lord, the water-carrier of the slaves of the Lord. ||3||
Attendant Nanak is God's servant, nay, the water-carrier of God's slaves.
Sri Guru Ji says: O Hari! I am the servant of the (panihari) water-carriers of him who is Your servant. ||3||
RR5B: Bhavai = may seem good (to You). Prabh = O Prabhu!
O Prabhu! We have come to Your shelter; now, as Your will may be, so save us (from evil deeds).
As it pleases You, You save me; I have come seeking Your Sanctuary, O God, O Lord King.
As it pleases You, so do You save me and I have sought Yours refuge, O Lord Master, the king.
O (Ram Raje) Prabhu! We have come into Your shelter; in whatever way it seems good to You, take us into Your shelter.
As it pleases You God, keep me. I have come to Your sanctuary, beloved God.
E8GQ: Bhuli = having gone astray, having taken the wrong road. Vigarah = we are spoiling our own life. Laj = honour. Hari = O Hari! Rakhae = rakhai, keep.
Day and night we go astray (from the road of life) and spoil (our own spiritual life). O Hari! Keep our honour.
I am wandering around, ruining myself day and night; O Lord, please save my honor!
I am straying and spoiling myself day and night. O God, save You my honour.
We, going astray from Your hukam, spoil night and day — that is to say, we commit sins; do You keep my honour.
I stray from the path and ruin my life day and night, God, please protect my dignity (or honour).
B000: De = having given. Samjhae = samjhai, grant understanding.
O Prabhu! We are Your children, You are our Guru, You are our father; giving us understanding, grant us good sense.
I am just a child; You, O Guru, are my father. Please give me understanding and instruction.
I am child and You, O Guru, are my father. Do You instruct me and put me on the right track.
We are children and You are Guru and father. As one may be made to understand, so give us good sense and make us understand.
I am Your child, You are my Guru and Father, please give me Your wisdom and help me understand (how to live).
02AY: Kandhia = is said to be, is called. Paij = honour. Rakhae = rakhai, keep ||4||10||17||
O Hari! Servant Nanak is called Your servant; (show mercy, keep Your servant's) honour. ||4||10||17||
Servant Nanak is known as the Lord's slave; O Lord, please preserve his honor! ||4||10||17||
Servant Nanak is said to be the slave of God. So keep You his honour, O God.

Sri Guru Ji says: we are (kandhia) called Your servants; therefore, O Hari! Keep my (paij) pledge, or Your own pledge of loving the bhagats — before this too You have gone on keeping it. ||4||10||17||
Servant Nanak is known publicly as Your slave. God, please uphold my honour (reputation).
DWSJ: Mastaki = upon the forehead. Dhuri = from the very court.

Those men upon whose forehead Parmatma inscribes (the writ of meeting the Guru) from His very court, they meet the Guru; (from their minds, by the Guru's mercy) the darkness of unawareness of spiritual life is dispelled, and in their hearts the understanding of spiritual life granted by the Guru shines out.
Those who have the blessed pre-ordained destiny of the Lord written on their foreheads, meet the True Guru, the Lord King.
They alone. who have such a writ of God on their forehead, since the very beginning, them the True Guru meets.
O Hari Ram Raje! Those upon whose forehead You have inscribed a good writ from the very beginning, they have met the Satiguru.
ZWLK: Agianu = unawareness of spiritual life. Andhera = darkness. Ghati = in the heart. Balia = shone out.
(From their minds, by the Guru's mercy) the darkness of unawareness of spiritual life is dispelled, and in their hearts the understanding of spiritual life granted by the Guru shines out.
The Guru removes the darkness of ignorance, and spiritual wisdom illuminates their hearts.
The Guru removes their darkness of ignorance, and Divine Knowledge illumined in their heart.
The Satigur has cut away their darkness of agian, and again in their hearts the lamp of atam-gian has been lit.
AAYJ: Ladha = has been found. Padaratho = a precious thing. Bahuri = again. Chalia = was lost.
They find the precious jewel of Parmatma's Nam, which is never afterwards lost (by them).
They find the wealth of the jewel of the Lord, and then, they do not wander any longer.
They find the wealth of the jewel of God's Name and then wander not, again.
In the light of the lamp of gian they have found the jewel-treasure of Hari within this very antahkaran; then it has not become unsteady from that certainty.
HKK1: O servant Nanak! Those men who, taking the Guru's shelter, remember Parmatma's Nam — having remembered the Nam they are absorbed into Parmatma itself. ||1||
Servant Nanak meditates on the Naam, the Name of the Lord, and in meditation, he meets the Lord. ||1||
Servant Nanak has meditated on the Name and through meditation he has met the Lord.
Sri Guru Ji says: the servants have made the aradhan of the Nam; by that (aradhi) which is fit to be worshipped, or by the worshipping, Hari has been met. ||1||
XQZJ: Aisa = such a precious one. Se = those men. Kahe = for what? Jagi = in the world.
Such a precious Nam (which gives the understanding of spiritual life) — those men who have not remembered it, for what did they take birth in the world?
Those who have not kept the Lord's Name in their consciousness - why did they bother to come into the world, O Lord King?
They, who did not contemplate on such a Name of God, why did they come in this world?
O Ram Raje! Those who have not contemplated such a Hari-Nam, why have they come into the world — that is to say, they were born in vain.
VV9Q: Dulanbhu = durlabh, had only with great difficulty. Birtha = in vain. Sabhu = the whole.
This human birth is had only with great difficulty; without the simran of the Nam the whole of it goes to waste.
It is so difficult to obtain this human incarnation, and without the Naam, it is all futile and useless.
Very difficult to obtain is this human birth and without the Name, it all goes in vain.
This human birth is durlabh; without the Nam it goes in vain in every way.
VPQC: Huni = in this human birth. Vatai = at the season of tilth. Agai = in the world beyond, when the time has passed. Kia khae = what will he eat?
He who does not sow Parmatma's Nam in the fitting season (in the field of his own heart) within the human birth — how will he satisfy the hunger of the spiritual life?
Now, in this most fortunate season, he does not plant the seed of the Lord's Name; what will the hungry soul eat, in the world hereafter?
Now, in the opportune season, man sows not God's Name. What will the hungry eat, hereafter?
He who has not now sown the Nam in this (vatai) season — when hunger comes ahead in the next world, what will he eat? That is to say, only regret will remain in his hands.
S3GU: Manmukh = those who follow their own mind. Hari bhai = to Hari (this alone) seems good ||2||
O Nanak! (Say —) Those who follow their own mind get the round of births again and again; (for them) this alone is what Parmatma sees fit. ||2||
The self-willed manmukhs are born again and again. O Nanak, such is the Lord's Will. ||2||
The way-ward are born again. Such is the will of God, O Nanak.
Sri Guru Ji says: by this alone the manmukhs come to birth again; so it seems good to (hari bhae) Hari. ||2||
0MA7: Sabhu ko = every being. Sabhi = all.
O Hari! You are the Master of all beings; every being is Your (creation); all beings are created by You alone.
You, O Lord, belong to all, and all belong to You. You created all, O Lord King.
You, O God, belongest to all and all belong to You. My Master, the King, You have created all.
O Hari Ram Raje! You are the Master of all and they are Your servants; all are created by You alone.
72ZN: Hathi = in the hand. Chalahi = they walk, they move.
Nothing at all is in any being's own power; as You set them walking, so all beings walk.
Nothing is in anyone's hands; all walk as You cause them to walk.
Nothing, nothing is in the hands of any one. All walk as You drivest them.
In no one's hand is any thing at all, not even a little; all move as moved by You.
06NN: Piare = O Beloved! Tudhu = You. Mani = in the mind. Bhae = they seem good.
O Beloved! Those beings whom You unite with Yourself, those who seem good to You within Your own mind, they stay joined at Your feet.
They alone are united with You, O Beloved, whom You cause to be so united; they alone are pleasing to Your Mind.
My Beloved God, they alone unite with You, whom You unitest and who are pleasing to Your mind.
O beloved Hari! He whom You unite, he meets You; those who, O Hari! have seemed good to Your mind, they have met.
5G7U: Nami = by way of the Nam. Tarae = carries across ||3||
O servant Nanak! Those men to whom the Guru is met, the Guru joins them to Parmatma's Nam and carries them across (the world-ocean). ||3||
Servant Nanak has met the True Guru, and through the Lord's Name, he has been carried across. ||3||
Servant Nanak has met the True Guru, who, through God's Name, has floated him.
Sri Guru Ji says: those servants to whom by Your grace the Satigur has been met — O Hari, possessor of the Nam! them You have carried across. ||3||
8WA0: Gavai = sings the virtues. Ragi = ragin, by singing through the rags. Nadi = nadin, by sounding the conch and the rest. Bedi = bedin, by way of the religious books. Bahu bhanti kari = in many ways. Bhijai = is pleased.
One man sings by rag, another by sounding the conch and other instruments, another by reading the religious books — in many ways he sings Parmatma's virtues, but Parmatma is not pleased in this way.
Some sing of the Lord, through musical Ragas and the sound current of the Naad, through the Vedas, and in so many ways. But the Lord, Har, Har, is not pleased by these, O Lord King.
Some sing Lord God through music, musical instruments and religions books in various ways, but, by these methods, Master, the King is not pleased.

Some persons perform Your singing by (ragi) rags and by nads; some perform it by the chanting of the Ved; but O Hari! In this way they sing much and in many fashions. Without love You are not (bhijai) softened, that is to say You are not pleased.
1XN2: Antari = within. Kapatu = deceit. Roi = having wept.
Those within whom there is deceit and sin — what is the point of their lamenting?
Those who are filled with fraud and corruption within - what good does it do for them to cry out?
In whom are fraud and sin what good can bewailing do to them?
Those within whose antahkaran is the disease which is deceit — what will they accomplish by false weeping? That is to say, their weeping is false; or, what praise is there in their weeping?
F0LB: Siri rog = upon the head of the diseases. Hathu dijai = a hand be laid.
The Creator knows every matter (of every man's heart), even though a hand be laid over the inner diseases (even though the attempt be made to hide the inner vices).
The Creator Lord knows everything, although they may try to hide their sins and the causes of their diseases.
God, the Creator, knows everything, though man tries to hide his sin or source of disease.

O Hari Creator! You know everything. The (siri rog) chief of all diseases, the disease of agian, their deeds have placed in the hand which is their antahkaran. Or, as when there is a disease on the head — that is, baldness — and a hand is laid over it, still it is not hidden, so by weeping the disease which is deceit is not hidden. Or, He puts the chief disease of pride into the hand which is their mind.
N46V: Sudhu = pure. Gurmukhi = by taking the Guru's shelter ||4||11||18||
O Nanak! Those men whose heart becomes pure by taking the Guru's shelter, they alone perform Parmatma's bhagti, they alone take Hari's Nam. ||4||11||18||
O Nanak, those Gurmukhs whose hearts are pure, obtain the Lord, Har, Har, by devotional worship. ||4||11||18||
The pious persons, whose mind is pure, O Nanak, obtain Lord God's love-worship.
Sri Guru Ji says: O Hari! Those gurmukhs whose heart is pure, they take Your bhagti in every way. ||4||11||18||
WKCP: Antari = in the heart. Te jan = those men. Sugharh = of fitting conduct, of good mental formation.
Those men within whose heart the love of Parmatma is present — (in Parmatma's eyes) those men are of fitting conduct and are wise.
Those whose hearts are filled with the love of the Lord, Har, Har, are the wisest and most clever people, O Lord King.
Discreet and wise are the persons, within whose mind is the Lord God's love.
Those in whose antahkaran, by mind and speech, is the love of repeating the Nam of Ram Raje Hari Hari — those servants are (sugharh) fair and (siane) shrewd, or exceedingly shrewd.
ABA2: Bhuli = having erred. Chuki = having stumbled. Bhi = still. Khare = good. Bhane = they seem dear.
If they ever, erring and stumbling, utter (mistaken words) outwardly among people, still they seem good and dear to Parmatma.
Even if they misspeak outwardly, they are still very pleasing to the Lord.
Even if they outwardly err in speech, still they are very dear to God.
Although outwardly they (bhuli chuki) err and stumble in speech, (bhi) even so they have (khare) fully seemed (bhane) good to Hari.
WSN8: Parmatma's sants have no other support (apart from Parmatma); (they know that) Parmatma alone is the honour of the honourless.
The Lord's Saints have no other place. The Lord is the honor of the dishonored.
God's saints have no other place. God is the honour of the dishonoured.
To Hari's sants there is no other place apart from Hari, because the giver of honour to the honourless is Hari alone.
48DL: Dibanu = support, the place of appeal. Tanu = strength, strength of arm. Satane = strong, possessed of strength ||1||
O Nanak! For Parmatma's servants Parmatma's Nam alone is the support; Parmatma alone is their strength of arm, (on the strength of which, against the vices) they stay strong. ||1||
The Naam, the Name of the Lord, is the Royal Court for servant Nanak; the Lord's power is his only power. ||1||
The Name is the mainstay of slave Nanak, and through God's power he is powerful.
Sri Guru Ji says: to them the Nam alone is (dibanu) the support, because they, having obtained the (tan) strength of Hari alone, have become (satane) possessed of strength. ||1||
3J14: Jithai = at which place. Jai = having gone. Suhava = beautiful.
That place where the beloved Guru goes and sits becomes (for the Gursikhs) a beautiful place.
Wherever my True Guru goes and sits, that place is beautiful, O Lord King.
Wherever my True Guru goes and sits, beautiful is that place, O Lord, the King.
My Satiguru, who is the form of Ram Raje, wherever he goes and sits in visible form, or in whichever heart he goes and sits in the form of the updesh, that place becomes resplendent.
EQWT: Gursikhi = the Gursikhs have. Bhalia = found. Dhuri = dust. Mukhi = upon the face.
The Gursikhs find that place, and taking its dust they apply it to their own forehead.
The Guru's Sikhs seek out that place; they take the dust and apply it to their faces.
The Guru's disciples search out that site and take and apply the dust there of to there face.
The Gursikhs have searched out that very place, and taking the dust of that place they have applied it to the face.
RBYW: Ghal = labour. Thai pai = became accepted (at Prabhu's door).
Those Gursikhs who remember Parmatma's Nam — their labour (of seeking the Guru's place) is accepted at Parmatma's door.
The works of the Guru's Sikhs, who meditate on the Lord's Name, are approved.
The service of the Guru's Sikhs, who ponder on the Name is approved.
Those who have meditated upon the Hari Nam, the (ghal) service of those Gursikhs has (thai pai) become fruitful.
DCP5: Puj karava = has worship done. Karava = karai. Lava = lai. Dhiava = dhiaia ||2||
Nanak — those men who seat the honour and regard of the Guru (within their own heart), Parmatma has (their) honour done (in the world). ||2||
Those who worship the True Guru, O Nanak - the Lord causes them to be worshipped in turn. ||2||
They, who worship the True Guru, them the Lord causes to be worshipped.
Sri Guru Ji says: those who have performed the worship of the Satigurus, Hari has their worship performed by the whole world. ||2||
87M2: Mani = in the mind. Hari = O Hari!
O Hari! In the mind of the Guru's Sikhs Your love stays formed, the love of Your Nam stays settled,
The Guru's Sikh keeps the Love of the Lord, and the Name of the Lord, in his mind. He loves You, O Lord, O Lord King.
The Guru's Sikh, in his mind, has love for God and God's Name. He Loves You, O Lord God, the King.
O Hari Ram Raje! In the mind of the Gursikhs, in every way, for the sake of attaining You, is the love of repeating the Hari Nam.
